name: Villa Stein-de Monzie (Les Terrasses)
features: White box of strip windows set out with regulating lines; a canopy marks the door and a balcony the service entrance.

extras.file: File:Model of Villa Stein-de-Monzie, V&A London 01.jpg
File:Model of Villa Stein-de-Monzie, V&A London 03.jpg

view: street (north) elevation: three bands of strip windows, entrance canopy, small balcony over the service door
note: No free photo on Commons (France has no freedom of panorama; Le Corbusier died in 1965), only CC0 photos of a V&A model. The Fondation Le Corbusier text (via search) confirms strip windows, the awning over the entrance door and the balcony over the service door; the exact window lengths and door positions are drawn from memory of published elevations, so check against a photo. The garden side with its hanging terrace is not shown.

name: E-1027
features: Gray's white seaside house: pilotis, a long window band and ship-like balcony rails, with furniture she designed.
view: sea-side (south) elevation: upper floor with window band and balcony rail, part raised on pilotis, glazed stair cabin on the roof
note: Commons has no clear free exterior photo: two CC BY-SA 3.0 files (E1027 2013 01/02, 1280px) show restoration damage details, and File:Sea shore at Roquebrune.jpg (public domain) shows the villa only behind trees. Gray died in 1976 and France has no freedom of panorama. Sources confirm a flat-roofed two-storey white villa on pilotis with ribbon windows, white balcony rails with blue canvas awnings, terraces and a glazed cabin over the stair on the roof; the number and placement of pilotis and the cabin's position are my reading of published photos, not of a plan. Please compare with a photo before publishing; mark unsure if it doesn't match.

name: Climat de France
features: Vast stone housing estate; its main block (233 x 38 m) rings a courtyard lined by 200 pillars.
note: No free photo found: File:Climat De France 0136.jpg and 0137 Panini 6.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0) are described as 'Climat De France von Stephane Couturier', so they seem to show Couturier's artworks rather than the building itself; check before use. Sources give the size (233 x 38 m, 200 pillars round the courtyard, built 1954-57, now Oued Koriche) but not the storeys or how the pillars meet the flats, so I did not draw it.

Wikipedia gives no storeys or facade pattern, and residents have walled in most balconies, so I did not draw it.
